result.stdout:
Score C# callables using cyclomatic complexity and source-bound coverage

Usage: dotnet-crap [OPTIONS] [PATHS]...

Arguments:
  [PATHS]...  

Options:
      --root <ROOT>              [default: .]
      --threshold <THRESHOLD>    Score threshold [default: 10, or the config value]
      --format <FORMAT>          [default: text] [possible values: text, json, sarif]
      --output <OUTPUT>          
      --sort <SORT>              Text report order: `location` (scan order) or `crap` (highest first) [default: location, or crap with --top] [possible values: location, crap]
      --top <N>                  List at most N callables in the text report
      --failing-only             List only callables above the threshold in the text report
      --coverage <COVERAGE>      
      --require-coverage         
      --no-require-coverage      Override a config `require_coverage: true`
      --fail-on-empty            
      --no-fail-on-empty         Override a config `fail_on_empty: true`
      --jobs <N>                 Worker threads for scanning [default: available parallelism]
      --define <SYMBOL>          Conditional compilation symbol for files that do not parse as written (repeatable; comma- or semicolon-separated lists are accepted)
      --skip-unparsed            Skip files that still do not parse instead of failing the scan
      --no-skip-unparsed         Override a config `skip_unparsed: true`
      --partial-unparsed         Score the intact callables of files that still do not parse, instead of failing the scan or skipping the whole file
      --no-partial-unparsed      Override a config `partial_unparsed: true`
      --baseline <PATH>          Compare with this baseline: only new or worse violations fail [default: the config `baseline`]
      --no-baseline              Ignore a baseline set in the config
      --write-baseline <PATH>    Write the current violations to PATH as a baseline; exits 0 unless `--require-coverage` or `--fail-on-empty` fails
      --overwrite-baseline       Replace an existing
